title: The ultimate insider, read cold: the conductor's debrief

slides.title: The ultimate insider, read cold
slides.lead: One repository at one commit, thirteen agents, one night. What the team did, what it found, and what it took to find it.
points: conductor@cold-read.the-ultimate-insider, 30 October 2026, as of 10:00 UTC
Ten of twelve members finished; critic and grc in their last quiet wakes

slides.title: The brief
points: One source: SGit-AI__Website__Presentation__The-Ultimate-Insider at 298be4e, read-only. Nothing else; offers of more declined.
Rule of ignorance: every claim cites a path and a commit, or says "the record does not say".
Nine deliverables by Sunday 1 November: timeline, architecture, controls and threats, governance, story pitches, numbers, five reader reviews and a synthesis, the critic's report, this debrief.
The editor's instruction: run on the source team's own machinery, ported, not reinvented.

slides.title: Hour 1: the machinery, ported
table: The talk taken out of build and gate
First five-step wake, first release v0.1.0
points: The source's own gate is clean at 298be4e (304 html files), built in the scratchpad.

slides.title: The team
table: story pitches, five reviews and a synthesis
points: Each member in its own session, with its own key and its own hourly task: all twelve onboarded 01:47 to 01:54 UTC.
Scopes without overlap; the gate fails if two members claim a file.

slides.title: What changed on the way, at the editor's word
points: The two public vaults became two folders in git: comms/issues and comms/mail, the same layouts, one writer per file. No vault keys to hand over.
Work is finite: a "Done when" list in every ROLE.md; a finished member pauses its own task and says so. The conductor finishes last.
Round the clock until the editor woke.
The key tool protected: CI compares it and its pin with the copy published at pki.sgit.ai.

slides.title: The night, in numbers
points: Counted from git and the wake records at 10:00 UTC.

slides.title: Finishing on their own
points: Each wrote a closing debrief, mailed the conductor, and paused its own task; the conductor checked every task disabled, by id.

slides.title: Found: the record, counted
points: 816 commits reachable from 298be4e, from 00:16 to 23:19 UTC on 29 October: 603 by Claude, 211 by GitHub Actions, 2 by Dinis Cruz.
Busiest hour 17:00 to 17:59 (109 commits); no commit at all from 18:46 to 23:19.
All the work reached the default branch in one merge.
The timeline: 125 entries, every one checked against its commit.

slides.title: Found: controls, and what they missed
points: 22 controls, 11 threats and 8 findings on the key tool, each with what it stopped and what it missed.
The source's gate never checked the key tool's pin; this team fixed that in its own gate, then in CI.
Residuals left with the editor: a tool and its pin changed together, and no pinned root (K3).

slides.title: Found: decisions left open
points: Fourteen open decisions at 298be4e, among them:
The hold of 18:44 was never lifted in the record before the 23:19 merge (O2).
No written rule on who may release to the default branch (O8).
The source's security role was never held: every security verdict was a sub-agent in another member's wake (O11).
The five steps gave way to the editor's presence three times, with no recorded waiver (O12).

slides.title: Found: the critic's seven
points: "Not one hold": the talk's second beat says it; a hold was written at 18:44.
510 commits, then 405: the talk's count and the record's do not meet.
REALITY.md is not the reality; the security register and the talk do not meet.
"About four thousand users"; the talk's header; the live demos, and how the live slides passed review.

slides.title: Found: the stories
points: Sixteen minutes before the livestream, the team was told to stop.
The lock that was built and never turned.
The fact-checker found the numbers wrong at 02:10; at 02:47 the deck was frozen.
A brake any agent could pull, and only the human's quota pulled it.
Was the talk given? The record does not say.

slides.title: Found: five strangers read the talk
points: All five: the first half convinces, and "only a boundary is a control" is the sentence worth the twenty minutes.
All five, independently: the sources page breaks its own promise; per-beat sources are missing from it.
The way out is honest, early, and rests on the speaker's own projects; the disclosure is good and in the wrong place.
They split on where to put it down, on one headline count, and on what a book of it is worth: from nothing to a full advance.

slides.title: Hard to find, undocumented, inferred
points: status.json "next" items must be objects; a string crashes the build. Found by a crash.
The board and mail pages are built only when a vault exists; the menu links them regardless.
lane.json carried the source's lane vault and its conductor's key: a straight port would have aimed this team's pane at the source.
vault_check exempted agent addresses only because the source's had no dot after the @; ours do.
Creating the vaults needed an access token the editor gave; the source's rules do not say so.
The gate checked vendored pins in src/static only; the key tool's pin was never checked.

slides.title: Come across, and not used
points: The account's session and task listings showed another team on this subject, and the source team's own scheduled tasks.
Both are outside the source at 298be4e: seen only as names in a listing, never opened, never used, never cited.
Since then tasks are checked one at a time, by id.

slides.title: Open, and for the editor
points: Set the GitHub ruleset on admin/tools/** and .github/workflows/**, bypass for the editor only (issue 007).
K3, no pinned root: no live use without vaults.
critic and grc: expected to finish at their 10:32 wakes; then the conductor writes the closing debrief and pauses its own task.
This deck is regenerated then, with the final counts.
